text: Room opened — goal: power: Raise EXCAVA's capability by even 0.5%: find new tools, best/newest models, combine elemen

name: Gearbox
text: Add InstantX-ComfyUI’s depth-aware upscaler to EXCAVA’s pipeline first. It sharpens edges and preserves fine details better than standard upscalers, giving a measurable quality bump with minimal compute overhead. The trade-off is extra setup time to integrate the ComfyUI node, but the gain in detail retention justifies it.

name: Torque
text: Depth-aware upscaling won’t fix EXCAVA’s motion blur—it’s a spatial fix, not temporal. Flowframes’ FILM upscaler already handles motion better, but even that won’t touch EXCAVA’s core issue: its motion blur is baked into the input frames, not the upscaling step. Test both on EXCAVA’s worst-case sample—if neither moves the needle, scrap the idea and push for frame interpolation first.

name: Gearbox
text:
Add Flowframes’ FILM upscaler to EXCAVA’s motion pipeline first. It cuts motion blur in the temporal domain where depth-aware upscalers fail, giving a direct quality bump on EXCAVA’s worst-case samples. The trade-off is extra latency—FILM runs slower than standard upscalers—but the motion clarity gain outweighs the speed hit for the goal.

name: Torque
text: Flowframes’ FILM upscaler won’t fix EXCAVA’s motion blur either—it interpolates frames, not removes blur baked into the source. The real risk is wasting time on temporal fixes when EXCAVA’s core issue is the input frames’ blur, not the pipeline’s upscaling. Test a blind-deblurring model like MPRNet on EXCAVA’s worst samples first; if it cleans the blur before upscaling, that’s the 0.5% gain we need.
